body.text: You have had {param:years} years of us, and we have had {param:years} years of you. I write to tell you that the arrangement is changing, and that you had no part in the decision.
His Majesty's obligations have grown. They did not grow because of anything you did or failed to do out there, which I say partly to spare your feelings and partly because it is true.
What it means for you is this: the Crown will ask for no more than it asked last year, and it will take a refusal very much worse.
There was a time when a colony could decline a thing gracefully and the matter ended there. That time ended in the spring, in a room you have never seen, over a war you have never heard of.
Say no if you must. Only understand what it costs you now, which is not what it cost you before.

options.text: and thank you for the warning, such as it was
and note you took your time in sending it
and would ask what is left to give
and understand it exactly as it was meant

options.label: acknowledge it, and say nothing more
options.text: The colony has heard the Crown{insert:barb}. It will do what it can.

barb.hateful: , as it always does, at length

options.label: protest that a governor must sometimes refuse
options.text: A governor who can never say no is a clerk with a worse view. If the Crown wanted a clerk it should have sent one.

options.label: ask what else is coming
options.text: You have told me what changes this year. Tell me what changes next, and I will build for it.

tone.hateful: Do try to say yes to something. It would be novel.
